description:
PC optimizer and AI voice assistant for Windows

FixKon cleans up Windows and keeps it fast, and answers when you talk to it.

It finds what is filling your drive by reading the NTFS index directly, so
searching every file on the disk takes about a second. It shows you exactly
which files it will clear before it clears them, sends your own files to the
Recycle Bin, shows which programs are slowing your
boot, removes the folders and registry keys other uninstallers leave behind,
and reads your PC's real health from Windows itself - SMART status, memory
speed against its rated speed, and the crash history behind Reliability
Monitor.

Hold Win+Alt and talk to it. FixKon sees your screen, points at what to click,
and can carry out multi-step tasks across your PC and connected accounts. Every
change it makes is recorded with its inverse, so "undo everything from the last
hour" is a real command.

Every PC tool is free and manual. A plan lets FixKon run them on a schedule.
Ask FixKon how to do something and it shows you. It flies to the control,
labels it, and waits for you to click it before moving on to the next step.
It never touches your mouse, so a walkthrough runs at your pace rather than
on a timer. Ask it to do the thing instead and it just does it, as before.

It teaches inside other programs too, not only Windows. Software that draws
its own interface, like music and design applications, used to leave it with
nothing to point at. It now reads the screen and points anyway.

You can change your mind part way. Say "just do it" while being shown and it
takes over; say "show me" while it is working and it walks you through
instead. If you get stuck on a step it offers to do that part for you rather
than pointing at the same button again.

Guide mode is now enforced by the app itself, so when it is on FixKon cannot
change anything on your PC whatever it is asked. Previously the setting
changed a label and nothing else.

The assistant speaks beside your cursor: what it is listening to, working on
or saying now appears next to the pointer and moves with it.

There are three voices, James, Tori and Brian. Choosing the second one
previously fell back to the first.
